text: wait who changed the layoutlm preprocessing pipeline on main? the bounding box coordinates are completely shifted on my local run

oh that was me. synced with priya earlier but maybe i should have pinged the channel. we decided to switch the backbone to a multi-modal flow matching architecture because vanilla vit was completely failing on rotated scanned invoices
but it broke the dataset split script! it is looking for absolute paths now or something?
off topic but is anyone down for coffee? getting a cold brew in 5 mins
no i literally just fixed that. merged the relative path fix into main commit a8c3e2f so just pull that and it will run fine. anyway the results are worth it
ok fine just pulled it. tracking looks normal now. wait wow the training baseline actually hit 91.2 percent f1 score on the validation set for table extraction? that actually beats production
told you. i put the full training script and logs in github.com/doc-parsing-org/core-ml/pull/412 if you want to review the loss curves
do you think i should change the max queue delay on the triton inference server from 10ms to 5ms for the staging environment?
i dont know, i dont think that affects the pipeline much. the bottleneck is elsewhere anyway
no! it does affect the pipeline, it will break the whole latency target if opencv resizing keeps maxing out the cpu on worker node 4 like it did this morning
wait did the node crash again? did you check the f1 race results from last weekend by the way? absolute chaos

no time for racing talk lol. it did not crash because i switched the worker configuration to utilize pillow-simd with libjpeg-turbo instead of stock opencv. memory usage dropped by 40 percent so throughput doubled. that is why i am tweaking triton now
ah damn okay that is a massive improvement. go ahead with the 5ms change then, let us keep latency under 45ms
cool, just shipped the updated triton dynamic batching configs to staging. let us see how it handles the next load test
i am losing my mind over this markdown serializer. complex text blocks keep losing their bold and italic formatting indicators during the regex parsing phase
regex is going to be a nightmare for structural document hierarchies anyway. did you look at the paper i dropped yesterday?
which one? you drop like five papers a week jensen
this one arxiv.org/abs/2303.12345 they use a graph neural network edge classification trick to preserve inline text attributes during structural parsing. exactly what you are fighting with
random question, did anyone see a mechanical watch in the small meeting room? think i left it on the desk

yeah i have it diego, will bring it over. and jensen, wow, okay this gnn edge parsing block actually works. implemented a variant of it in commit 4f6b12a and the inline token relationship errors vanished
just completed the final integration tests for the whole tables-to-markdown module too. officially launched the parsing patch to the beta branch
